I found one bug in the uncommitted changes, at `src/middleware/compress/index.ts:14`.

When `options.encoding` is set, the middleware no longer checks the client's `Accept-Encoding` header. The new code is `options?.encoding ?? ENCODING_TYPES.find(...)`. If the option is set, the `??` skips the header check entirely.

For example, `compress({ encoding: 'gzip' })` on a request with no `Accept-Encoding` header, or one that only lists `deflate`, still gzips the body and sets `Content-Encoding: gzip`. That client gets content it can't decode. The old code matched the option against the header, so it skipped compression when they didn't agree.

A fix would be to compress only when the header includes the chosen encoding. For example, filter `ENCODING_TYPES` by the option first, then run `find` against `accepted`.

I only reviewed `src/`. I didn't open the matching change in `deno_dist/middleware/compress/index.ts`, which is probably a generated copy with the same bug. I also didn't run any tests.

findings.summary: When options.encoding is set, the client's Accept-Encoding header is no longer checked, so responses are compressed even if the client doesn't accept that encoding.
findings.failure_scenario: compress({encoding:'gzip'}) with a request lacking Accept-Encoding (or only 'deflate'): encoding resolves to 'gzip' via ?? short-circuit, the body is gzipped and Content-Encoding: gzip is set, so the client receives undecodable content. The old code matched the option against the header and skipped compression on no match.
